    16  # Rectangular boxes in `ℝⁿ`
    17  
    18  In this file we define rectangular boxes in `ℝⁿ`. As usual, we represent `ℝⁿ` as the type of
    19  functions `ι → ℝ` (usually `ι = Fin n` for some `n`). When we need to interpret a box `[l, u]` as a
    20  set, we use the product `{x | ∀ i, l i < x i ∧ x i ≤ u i}` of half-open intervals `(l i, u i]`. We
    21  exclude `l i` because this way boxes of a partition are disjoint as sets in `ℝⁿ`.
    22  
    23  Currently, the only use cases for these constructions are the definitions of Riemann-style integrals
    24  (Riemann, Henstock-Kurzweil, McShane).
    25  
    26  ## Main definitions
    27  
    28  We use the same structure `BoxIntegral.Box` both for ambient boxes and for elements of a partition.
    29  Each box is stored as two points `lower upper : ι → ℝ` and a proof of `∀ i, lower i < upper i`. We
    30  define instances `Membership (ι → ℝ) (Box ι)` and `CoeTC (Box ι) (Set <| ι → ℝ)` so that each box is
    31  interpreted as the set `{x | ∀ i, x i ∈ Set.Ioc (I.lower i) (I.upper i)}`. This way boxes of a
    32  partition are pairwise disjoint and their union is exactly the original box.
    33  
    34  We require boxes to be nonempty, because this way coercion to sets is injective. The empty box can
    35  be represented as `⊥ : WithBot (BoxIntegral.Box ι)`.
    36  
    37  We define the following operations on boxes:
    38

    41    `(I : Set (ι → ℝ)) ⊆ J`;
    42  * `Lattice` instances on `WithBot (BoxIntegral.Box ι)`;
    43  * `BoxIntegral.Box.Icc`: the closed box `Set.Icc I.lower I.upper`; defined as a bundled monotone
    44    map from `Box ι` to `Set (ι → ℝ)`;
    45  * `BoxIntegral.Box.face I i : Box (Fin n)`: a hyperface of `I : BoxIntegral.Box (Fin (n + 1))`;
    46  * `BoxIntegral.Box.distortion`: the maximal ratio of two lengths of edges of a box; defined as the
    47    supremum of `nndist I.lower I.upper / nndist (I.lower i) (I.upper i)`.
    48

    50  that returns the box `⟨l, u, _⟩` if it is nonempty and `⊥` otherwise.
